text: C.2 Multi-Round and Self-Play Update In our loss function Eqn. , we introduce a reference model p θ ref p_{\theta_{\text{ref}}} , which is initialized from the student model p θ p_{\theta} . Following the setup of prior work ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) , we adopt a multi-round refinement strategy for training. Formally, this process can be written as: Round ​ n : ⋯ → p θ n − 1 ∗ ⏟ Reference → σ ⁡ ( β ​ log ⁡ p θ n p θ n − 1 ∗ ) ⏟ Discriminator \displaystyle\text{Round }n:\quad\cdots\;\rightarrow\;\underbrace{p_{\theta^{*}_{n-1}}}_{\text{Reference}}\;\rightarrow\;\underbrace{\sigma\!\left(\beta\log\tfrac{p_{\theta_{n}}}{p_{\theta^{*}_{n-1}}}\right)}_{\text{Discriminator}} Round n + 1 : → p θ n ∗ ⏟ Reference → ⋯ \displaystyle\text{Round }n+1:\quad\rightarrow\;\underbrace{p_{\theta^{*}_{n}}}_{\text{Reference}}\;\rightarrow\;\cdots where θ n − 1 ∗ \theta^{*}_{n-1} denotes the best-performing student model obtained in round n n . In each round, the reference model serves as a fixed generator. In our experiments, we update the reference model every 10 global steps, which corresponds to one round in our training schedule.
